avoid.reason: Pickpocketing around the Duomo, Centrale station and on the metro

hood_desc: The historic heart of the city, dominated by the great Gothic cathedral and the glittering Galleria shopping arcade, buzzing with tourists, luxury boutiques and grand piazzas. Ideal for first-time visitors who want landmarks and high-end shopping at their doorstep.

An elegant, artsy old quarter of cobbled lanes, galleries, antique shops and buzzing aperitivo bars, long associated with bohemians and the fashion crowd. Suits visitors who love charm, nightlife and boutique browsing.

A lively canal district lined with bars, trattorias and vintage shops that comes alive at aperitivo hour and into the night. Best for younger travelers and anyone chasing Milan's social, waterside evening scene.

A gleaming modern business and lifestyle district of skyscrapers, the Bosco Verticale towers and the Corso Como shopping strip. Great for those who want contemporary design, sleek dining and a polished urban feel.

A formerly working-class neighborhood turned hip and creative, full of independent bars, restaurants and a leafy, village-like feel. Appeals to a design-savvy, local crowd seeking authenticity away from the tourist core.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink and closely monitored.

transit.pay: Tap a contactless credit/debit card or Apple/Google Pay directly at ATM metro gates, trams, and buses - fares auto-cap at the daily rate after several taps. A single ticket costs €2.20 (~$2.40) and can also be bought at machines, tobacconists, or the ATM app.
transit.hours: Metro runs about 6am-12:30am (until 1:30am Saturdays); night bus lines substitute once the metro closes.
